name: Parian statuary
summary: Unglazed white porcelain that copies marble, cast in moulds as statuettes and busts. Victorian potters made it for the home, from copies of known sculpture to sentimental and literary figures.

philosophy.core_thesis: Fine sculpture comes into the Victorian parlour when a white porcelain slip is cast in a mould and fired without a glaze: marble, but small and cheap.
design_principles: Cast the figure in plaster moulds from a thin, creamy slip of parian paste.
Fire the figure unglazed at about 1200 °C, so that the surface looks like Parian marble.
Take the subject from a known sculpture: a Greek Slave, a Dorothea, a Venus, a bust of a poet or a queen.
Make the figure 20 to 60 cm high, and the bust 20 to 40 cm.
Keep the surface smooth and waxy, with a faint orange-peel grain.
Give detail with sharp relief: curls, laurel, lace and drapery, in shallow depth.
Add a coloured glaze or a little tinted slip only as a ground, never over the flesh.
Mark the base with the maker, the sculptor and the date of the registry.
anti_patterns: A glossy glaze over the figure
A bright enamel painting on the dress
A rough earthenware body with visible grain
A pose in rococo S-curves with lace dipped in slip
A cartoon figure with a flat, printed face
A grey or brown clay colour

form.shape: Statuettes of classical, historical and sentimental subjects, busts of the famous and small groups, with a base or a pedestal.
form.profile: A smooth, closed outline in a classical stance, with a column, a trunk or a rock to support the weight.
form.foot_and_rim: A round or square plinth with a moulded edge, often hollow, with a vent hole and a mark on the underside.
form.proportion: Height 20 to 60 cm; the wall is 3 to 6 mm thick, and the proportions are those of the marble original at a reduced scale.
rules: Reduce a known marble in scale and keep its pose.
Keep the seams fine and hide them in folds.
Show the sculptor and the maker on the base.

bodies.rule: Use a feldspar-rich porcelain paste that is cast as a thin slip and fires to a fine, waxy surface with a faint cream tone.

methods: piece moulding of heads and limbs
joining of cast parts with slip
fettling of seams with a knife
forming.joins: The parts of the figure are cast in moulds and joined with slip while still wet. The seams are cut back and sponged smooth.
forming.details: A fine orange-peel grain on the surface, a vent hole in the plinth, and a mark of the maker and the sculptor on the base.

glaze.pattern: The pattern is the form of the sculpture itself. A little gilt or tint, a glazed inside for a vessel, and sprigged flowers or laurel are the only additions.
glaze.gloss: Matt to waxy, 5 to 15 GU on the unglazed parian; a glazed inside is about 80 GU.
glaze.wear: The surface collects dust and yellow stains in the grain. It marks easily with oil, and the fine fingers and the edges break.

palette.strategy: A single warm white that copies marble, with soft grey shadow and a faint cream in the high light.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle oven, with the figures in saggars for a single firing.
processes: optional glaze or tint on the inside or the base
firing.scale: A factory process with moulders and finishers. Large firms made hundreds of models, and series for Art Union sales.
firing.signs: An orange-peel grain, a vent hole in the plinth, hidden seams and a maker's mark.

pieces.form: Reduced copy of a nude Greek Slave on a round plinth
Bust of a queen with a diadem and a draped shoulder, on a socle
Sentimental group of a mother and a child with a column and a wreath
Dorothea, a seated girl with a jar, taken from a known sculpture
Hound lying on a base with a gilt collar

positive: reduced copy of a classical sculpture
sharp shallow relief in curls and drapery

emotion.target_response: A sober, improving calm: the viewer sees white marble in small form and feels the taste, the culture and the order of a Victorian parlour.

use_cases: a museum or auction label for a parian figure
a prop of a white statuette on a shelf
a brief for a marble-look reproduction
avoid_when: the brief wants a coloured, glazed figure
the brief needs a cheap folk figure
the brief wants an art piece with a hand mark

modifiers.how: Change to a soft-paste body, cut the scale to 15 to 40 cm and take the subject from a pastoral painting.
Change to an earthenware body with a lead glaze and bold flat enamel colours, and add a name on the base.
